beats.label: S1 · Ambush in Leith Park
beats.text: A masked gunman ambushes DCI Carl Morck and his team at a crime scene, killing PC Anderson, paralysing DI James Hardy, and leaving Carl traumatised and guilt-ridden.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Carl's trauma, James's injury, and the still-open Leith Park shooting that shadows the whole season.

beats.label: S1 · Exiled to the basement
beats.text: Chief Superintendent Moira Jacobson banishes Carl to a derelict basement to launch cold case unit Department Q, where civilian Akram Salim latches onto the 2020 disappearance of advocate Merritt Lingard.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the unit, the central case, and Akram as Carl's indispensable partner.

beats.label: S1 · Merritt alive in a chamber
beats.text: Unknown to anyone, Merritt has been held captive for four years inside a hyperbaric chamber, forced monthly to guess which of her prosecutions her abductors are avenging.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The ticking-clock premise; every investigative beat feeds back into her survival.

beats.label: S1 · A buried investigation
beats.text: Retracing Merritt's steps to Mhòr and rebuilding her caseload, Carl and Akram grow certain her disappearance was deliberately mishandled, with Lord Advocate Stephen Burns quietly obstructing the original enquiry.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shifts the case from missing-person to institutional corruption and plants the leverage Carl later uses on Burns.

beats.label: S1 · Finch and the Kirsty cover-up
beats.text: The team prove businessman Graham Finch pressured Burns into blocking informant Kirsty Atkins's testimony, and that Finch's chauffeur firm supplied the Leith Park getaway driver — tying both cases to the same criminal network.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explicitly links the shooting to Finch, keeping that thread live going into next season.

beats.label: S1 · The man in the cap is Lyle
beats.text: Merritt realises her captors are Ailsa Jennings and her son Lyle, who assumed the identity of reporter Sam Haig after killing him; they blame her for the death of Lyle's brother Harry years earlier on Mhòr.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveal that reframes every earlier lead and drives the rescue.

beats.label: S1 · Rescue and a blackmailed budget
beats.text: Carl is shot protecting Akram on Mhòr as Akram kills Lyle and frees Merritt; three months later Carl blackmails Burns for funding, a new car, and Akram's detective badge, while Moira eyes James for the still-unsolved Leith Park case.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the team's permanence and sets up next season's likely case handoff to James.

cliffhanger.text: Merritt is home and Lyle is dead, but the Leith Park ambush is still unsolved and its trail runs straight to Graham Finch's organisation. Carl has bought Department Q's future by holding Burns's corruption over his head, and James — now walking again — may be handed the case that nearly killed him.
questions: Who actually ordered the Leith Park hit, and can Finch be touched for it?
How long can Carl's blackmail of Burns hold before it turns on him?
Will James take the shooting case, and what happens when he starts pulling threads Carl couldn't?

characters.name: DCI Carl Morck
characters.line: Traumatised, prickly head of Department Q; guilty over Leith Park, now reluctantly bonded to his team and blackmailing the Lord Advocate to keep the unit alive.

characters.name: Akram Salim
characters.line: Former Syrian police officer turned civilian filing clerk whose instincts cracked the Lingard case; newly badged as a detective and Carl's closest ally.

characters.name: DI James Hardy
characters.line: Carl's partner, paralysed in the ambush and now walking on crutches after rehab; back at work and being considered for the Leith Park investigation.

characters.name: DC Rose Dickson
characters.line: Desk-bound detective folded into Department Q who proved herself on the Mhòr leads; the third permanent member of the team.

characters.name: Merritt Lingard
characters.line: Advocate rescued after four years in the hyperbaric chamber, reunited with her brother William; met Carl at the end without knowing he was the one who found her.

characters.name: CS Moira Jacobson
characters.line: Carl's boss who exiled him to the basement; now stuck with a unit that keeps embarrassing the Crown Office by succeeding.

characters.name: Lord Advocate Stephen Burns
characters.line: Merritt's old supervisor exposed as having buried her case under Finch's pressure; funding Department Q under duress to keep his corruption quiet.

characters.name: Graham Finch
characters.line: Businessman who ordered Kirsty Atkins's stabbing and whose chauffeur firm supplied the Leith Park getaway driver; still untouched by charges.

characters.name: Dr Rachel Irving
characters.line: Carl's former therapist, taken off his case after his boundary-crossing; a personal thread he keeps circling back to.

characters.name: Jasper
characters.line: Carl's teenage stepson, briefly threatened by Finch's men; relationship with Carl is tentatively mending.
